bibl.title: Intelligibility in microbial complex systems: Wittgenstein and the score of life

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the intelligibility of microbial (and biological) life: the epistemology of representing complex living systems, reframed through the metaphor of the genome as a 'score of life' rather than a 'book of life'
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: how to cross the epistemological gaps between the successive hierarchical levels of the complex system of life, and whether life can be rendered intelligible by reducing it to the genetic-genomic language
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a 'half-thinking, half-seeing' (HT-HS) strategy for complex biological systems: combining analysis of representations (genomes, scores) with a non-propositional experience of meaning, to move through legibility and imageability toward higher intelligibility
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critique
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: life and music can be shown but not thought: their representations (genomes, musical scores) are mere representations of obscure realities, and diversification of knowledge paradoxically reduces intelligibility
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: conceptual-analysis
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A general rule (the law of projection) lets an interpreter read a symphony out of a static score, and the same rule inverts to reconstruct the score from the sound on a gramophone record - the internal similarity that makes these transitions possible.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Wittgenstein's rule of translation projects the symphony into the language of the musical score and translates that language into the gramophone record, and runs in reverse.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A collection of small parts assembles to produce a qualitatively different larger whole - groove-pattern to music, genes to a bacterial cell, cells to an ecological community.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Reproduction of a bacterial organism or a string quartet depends entirely on its representation (genome or score), while the higher living level leads by selecting the representation.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Understanding a complex system combines analysis of its representation (half-thinking) with a non-propositional experience of meaning that can only be seen or shown (half-seeing).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Analysis of scores and genomic sequences yields mechanistic, phylogenetic and evolutionary insight, but not the real dynamics or nature of music and life, which remain unthinkable.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Following Wittgenstein, the meaning of the word 'life' can only be shown, not understood, and consequently cannot be clearly expressed in propositions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In the absence of correct interpretation, a music score cannot be differentiated from a random sequence of notes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Systems Biology models are insufficient by themselves for full intelligibility, because deducing models of function from a complex system's behaviour is an inverse problem that is impossible to solve.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Validating models by comparing them with 'reality' may be a circular problem, since 'reality' can only be defined by models.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: representation → reproduction
span.note: A trans-hierarchical cyclic correlation ties representation to reproduction, produced blindly in both senses.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: music → the will of life
span.note: Reinterpreting Schopenhauer, the will represented in music is a representation of the will of life; a common will is independently perceived in both.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: genome → life
span.note: The life of a particular bacterial organism is, to a certain extent, represented in the organization of its genome, as a Mozart quartet is represented in its score.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: lower levels → higher levels
span.note: It is tempting to propose that the lower levels of the hierarchy blindly 'represent' the higher levels, though the higher levels categorically impose organisations on the lower.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: score → genetic language
span.note: In the central analogy, reading the score corresponds to reading the genetic language, producing music as reading the genome produces life.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: reading - human/sequential sense: a text read in one way only, sequentially, involving all characters
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: reading - cellular/genomic sense: genetic texts 'read' by cellular mechanisms in several different ways, each using a different selection of characters while skipping others
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: intelligibility - linguistic-theory sense: the trade-off between hierarchical levels in a shared world (Komarova and Niyogi)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: intelligibility - the authors' epistemological sense: the construction of meaningful (thinkable) models reflecting complex natural systems
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: representation - Wittgenstein's picture sense: a proposition/picture sharing a logical form with the fact it represents
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: representation - Schopenhauer's sense: music as a copy of the will itself, resembling an original reality that cannot be copied
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: representation - biological sense: genomic sequences representing life, meaningful only when a living system is present
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: score - musical sense: the notation from which a symphony can be reconstructed by a general rule (Tractatus 4.0141)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: score - 'score of life' sense: the genomic language, proposed as a better image than the book of life
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: will - Schopenhauer's metaphysical sense: the will itself, of which music is a copy and the Ideas its objectivity
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: harmony - sensibility-relative sense: an ordered score follows rules of harmony, yet that harmony may be totally useless for a different sensibility and out of any aesthetic possibility
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → Wittgenstein's Tractatus logico-philosophicus (theorem 4.0141 and the picture theory of representation)
span.note: The essay takes the Tractatus as its main post-Kantian framework for the limits of knowledge of the natural world.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → Schopenhauer's account of music as a copy of the will (The World as Will and Representation)
span.note: The will represented in music is read as a representation of the will of life.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → Dennis Noble's 'music of life' metaphor
span.note: The essay extends Noble's music-of-life idea to the intelligibility of microbial life.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → Maynard Smith and Szathmary's theory of major evolutionary transitions
span.note: Major transitions between hierarchical levels frame the score-to-music and genes-to-life passages.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contrasts-with → the classic 'book of life' metaphor for the genome
span.note: The 'score of life' is proposed as a better image of the genomic language.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: recommends → developing complex models of complex systems through convergent, multidisciplinary 'Big Science'
span.note: The half-seeing part needs more powerful model tools integrating all the -omics data.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: score of life —contrasted-with→ book of life
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.85 — Differentiator stated: sequential single reading versus multiple simultaneous cellular readings.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Increasing diversification and complexity in microbiology paradoxically results in a strong reduction of the intelligibility of microbial life.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The 'score of life' is a better image of the genomic language than the classic 'book of life', because genetic texts are read by cellular mechanisms in several different ways rather than sequentially.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Both life and music can be shown but not thought; genomic sequences and musical scores are mere representations of these obscure realities.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A strategy of half-thinking and half-seeing is needed to expand knowledge of complex systems such as life and music.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The epistemological process for complex biological systems has three phases: legibility, imageability, and intelligibility.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the construction of meaningful (thinkable) models in response to the assimilation of knowledge, able to reflect to some extent the reality of complex natural systems
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a series of staves on which all the instrumental and/or vocal parts of a musical work are written in vertical alignment so the parts may be read simultaneously

span.label: the descriptive level of anatomy and physiology - the composition of Wittgensteinian atomic facts and propositions

span.label: the stage at which a holistic, physiognomically comparable image of a living structure can be seen or shown
